subject: [PATCH for-7.5 5/5] memcg: simplify high limit handling after a charge

2026-10-10.patch_summary: This patch simplifies the handling of high limits in memory cgroups by separating the hierarchy scan from high-limit enforcement. It introduces a new variable to track whether the task is running in user context, and uses this information to determine whether to queue high_work or record the task's overage after scanning the hierarchy. The patch also clarifies comments and removes redundant code, but does not introduce any functional changes.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Michal Hocko noted that the patch does not handle the case where a task is in a cgroup with memory.high set and also has a local charge, which can lead to inconsistent behavior.

Reviewer Michal Hocko suggested simplifying the code by immediately returning if no cgroup is found to be over the high limit, instead of continuing with the rest of the function.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sat 10-10-26 14:09:57, Shakeel Butt wrote:
[...]

---

Would it be much simpler to bail out on iter==NULL (i.e. nothing over
high limit) right after the loop?

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that removing the NULL check for iter would skip a potential call to __mem_cgroup_handle_over_high(), but wants to preserve current behavior and plans to address this in a follow-up series.
reviews.raw_body:
I want this patch to not change any behavior. If we return here when iter is
NULL, we will skip a potential call to __mem_cgroup_handle_over_high() when
current->memcg_nr_pages_over_high > MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH. Though I agree that is
very subtle and most probably unexpected. If we decide to remove it, we should
do it in a separate patch. Actually I am working on a followup series where I
plan to remove the sync enforcement of memory.high and put high enforcement on
the code paths which can potentially do a lot of allocation within a single
kernel entry.

2026-10-14.patch_summary: This patch simplifies the handling of high limits in memory cgroups by separating the hierarchy scan from high-limit enforcement. It introduces a new variable to track task context and uses it to determine whether to use worker contexts or not. The patch also clarifies comments, removes redundant code, and keeps the synchronous pending-overage check independent of the scan result. No functional changes are intended.
